goal: A blocked step that waits for a time, for an earlier step's deploy plus a delay, or for another project to be done becomes `ready` by itself. Nobody has to notice and run `mc step ready`.

Today `blocked_by` is `{ kind, name }` with `kind` one of `decision | project | workarea` (`src/mc/plan-schema.js:50`). A blocked step is a person's (ruling 21), and the runner never reads `deploys.tsv` when it decides what is ready. `staleBlockers` (`src/mc/stale-blockers.js:58`) notices that a `project` blocker is done, but by design it writes nothing, so the step still waits for a person.

success_criteria.criterion: The plan schema, the register and `mc step blocked` accept `time` and `deploy` blockers with their fields, and refuse a malformed one.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/plan-schema.test.js`, `tests/mc/register.test.js` (the fields survive `normaliseEntry` and `patchStep`) and `tests/mc/step-command.test.js` (or the test beside `commands/step.js`): `--until`, `--after-deploy`, `--hours`; a past `--until` is refused, as is `--after-deploy` on a memoro-cli step and `--after-deploy` naming the step itself or a later one.

success_criteria.criterion: A due blocker is released by the runner's `queue()` into `ready` with a comment, and one that is not due is left blocked.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/step-release.test.js`: `time` before and after `at`; `deploy` with no deployed row, a row that does not contain the sha, a row that contains it but is younger than `hours`, and one that is old enough; `project` done, not done, and not on main. `tests/mc/run.test.js` (or the runner test that drives `queue()`): a due step comes out of `queue()` as `ready`, and its register entry carries the comment.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc step <project>` and the page say how long a time or deploy wait has left.
success_criteria.check: The `mc step` test: `on deploy of step 3 + 24h — 7h40m left`, `on deploy of step 3 — not deployed yet`, `until 2026-10-14 08:00Z — 3d left`. The page test for the blocked line shows the same words.

success_criteria.criterion: Live: a step is released by the runner on the new code.
success_criteria.check: The close-out quotes the `runner.log` line for the first release after the runner runs step 2's code, together with that step's register comment. If no release has happened by then, the close-out says so in its comments instead of inventing one.

steps.title: 1. time and deploy blockers in the schema, the register and mc step blocked, and the pure rule for when one is due
steps.done_when: `BLOCKER_KINDS` holds `time` and `deploy`. The schema, `normaliseStep` and `patchStep` accept and keep `at`, `step` and `hours`. `mc step blocked` takes `--until <iso>` and `--after-deploy [<n>] [--hours <h>]`. A new `src/mc/step-release.js` exports a pure `blockerDue(step, context)` and `describeWait(step, context)`. `mc step <project>` prints the wait. The tests in success criteria 1 and 3 are green, and so is `npm test`.
comments: For step 2: in step-release.js, stepsOf() takes no argument and returns this project's register steps; the deploy step is stepsOf()[step-1]. contains(sha, rowSha) means sha is an ancestor of rowSha. describeWait gives 'on project y — not done / not on main' only when context.plans is passed. mc step <project> (commands/step.js waitContext) shows how much time is left only for time and deploy blockers.

steps.title: 2. The runner releases due blockers in queue(), and the page shows the wait
steps.done_when: The runner's `queue()` (`src/mc/run.js:2414`) releases every current blocked step whose blocker is due: the register step becomes `ready` with the comment `Released <now>: <why>` and a `runner.log` line. Released steps come out of `queue()` as `ready` the same call. `staleBlockers` no longer reports a `project` blocker that is done. The page's blocked line uses `describeWait`. The tests in success criterion 2 are green, and so is `npm test`.
comments: The page shows a deploy wait without its time left (on deploy of step N + Hh): working it out needs git ancestry in memoro's checkout, and that would be a git call per paint. mc step <project> shows the time left. The release takes effect only after mc run --update, and criterion 4 (live) is the close-out's to quote.

steps.title: 3. Close-out
steps.done_when: The runner runs step 2's code, every criterion is marked with what was measured, `docs/technical/mc-run.md` describes the self-releasing blockers, `docs/project/project_log.md` has the row, and every step is `done` with its PR.
